A test that needs a fixture

CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR makes the path independent of where cargo test is run from.

A test that needs a temp dir

Testing a trait with a hand-written fake

Injecting the clock is the single highest-value testability change you can make. It removes sleep() from tests and makes expiry deterministic.

A mock with mockall

A property test instead of 20 examples

The generator is constrained to printable ASCII — a property test with an unconstrained input is usually testing the wrong thing.

A snapshot test for output that is hard to assert on

Snapshots are the right tool for CLI output, rendered HTML and JSON payloads — anything where writing assertions by hand is busywork.

A database test with a real database

#[sqlx::test] creates a fresh database per test and runs migrations. Never mock the database layer — you end up testing your mock.

An HTTP handler test with no network

oneshot runs the whole router — extractors, middleware, error mapping — in process, in microseconds.

A CLI test that checks exit codes

What to test, ranked

  1. The invariant that would cost money — money nets to zero, a ledger balances.
  2. The boundary — empty input, one element, the maximum, invalid UTF-8.
  3. The error path — every Err variant is reachable and carries the right data.
  4. The regression — one test per bug you fix, named after the bug.

Line coverage is a weak signal. Mutation testing (cargo mutants) tells you whether your tests would notice a change at all.
